corrected_count.measured_so_far: the seven headings were repaired and the set is 99. The six are still in, so 99 - 6 = 93 is what the repair would leave.
corrected_count.status: a prediction to be checked, not a target to reach. If reading a second and a third filing shows the Item 8 proxy has to be narrowed differently, the number follows from the corrected scope - it does not constrain it. An implementation tuned until it emits 93 for Pfizer would satisfy this line and prove nothing.

in_scope_missed.consequence: blocks 3859-3864 lose their Comirnaty heading, 3871-3872 lose Paxlovid, 3883-3885 lose Asbestos, 3887-3888 lose Docetaxel, 3890-3891 and 3897-3898 lose Zantac, 3900 loses Chantix. in_scope_missed.the_inconsistency_that_makes_it_visible: Orgovyx (relugolix), Eliquis (apixaban), Oxbryta (voxelotor), Nurtec (rimegepant) and Xtandi (enzalutamide) are all kept. The difference is that their generic name in parentheses pushes them over twelve characters. Whether a product heading survives depends on how long its generic name is, which is not a rule anyone would write down.

the_auditor_s_critical_audit_matter.how_they_got_in: not by a rule about speakers. ITEM_8 - the whole financial statements section, audit report included - is scanned as a stand-in for the definition's 'contingencies notes'. That proxy is the cause.
the_auditor_s_critical_audit_matter.the_argument_that_holds: document part, supported by content. The approved source names three places: Item 3, the legal proceedings section, and the contingencies notes. The audit report is none of them. And the content agrees: block 1884 is 1,233 characters of audit procedures - 'We evaluated the design and tested the operating effectiveness of certain internal controls ... We read letters received directly from the Company's external and internal legal counsel' - which is not a legal proceeding; block 1882 restates what Notes 1S and 16 say, and Note 16A is already taken in full, so it adds no disclosure while mixing in a second document part.
the_auditor_s_critical_audit_matter.the_argument_that_was_wrong: the first version of this finding said the Spec's entity_scope is registrant and the auditor's report is therefore out. That does not follow and the review was right to refuse it. entity_scope answers which entity the disclosure concerns, not who is speaking, and block 1882 - now archived whole - is squarely about the registrant: 'the Company is involved in product liability and other product-related litigation ... Certain of these pending ... could result in losses that could be substantial.' A rule that excluded it for being in the auditor's voice would exclude a disclosure about the registrant.
the_auditor_s_critical_audit_matter.what_they_are: the independent registered public accounting firm's critical audit matter, 'Evaluation of product liability and other product-related litigation', inside the audit report at the front of Item 8.

question: Are Pfizer's 92 D02 excerpts the 92 that should be taken? A frozen Run, an Evidence PASS and a published row answer whether the machinery worked, not whether the content is right.

out_of_scope_still_taken.why_not_yet: the cause is that ITEM_8 is scanned as a proxy for the contingencies notes the definition names. Narrowing it changes every filing's set and one filing has been read. Inventing a rule for where the auditor's report ends from a single example is the mistake this whole exercise exists to avoid.

rules._note_heading: inside a located note scope, an emphasized unlinked block carrying a letter is content even under twelve characters
rules._page_furniture: a repeated block is furniture only when the block before or after it also repeats - furniture travels in company

what_is_correct: every substantive paragraph of Note 16A is present and in document order
the scope boundary [3821, 3937) is right: B guarantees, C commitments, D contingent consideration and E insurance all begin at or after 3937 and none appears in the set

the 25 running-header blocks - 'Pfizer Inc.', '2025 Form 10-K', the page number, 'Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements', 'Pfizer Inc. and Subsidiary Companies', repeated five times - are all correctly excluded
the two in-scope items outside the sub-note, 2302 (the contingencies note lead-in) and 2351 (the Seagen legal matters bullet), are correctly included
what_this_changes_now: the coordinate is registered as defective and withdrawn from current delivery. business_content_accepted was already false everywhere; this replaces 'not checked' with 'checked and wrong in six places and short in seven'.
what_this_does_not_do: change the approved definition - each item was judged against it, not against a new one
repair the selector, which is a separate change with its own measurements
say anything about the other eight companies' D02 sets, which have not been read

where_the_92_come_from.note: NOTE_16_SUB_A is nested inside ITEM_8, so the two are not additive. ITEM_3's single block is the 77-character hyperlink already registered as a separate defect.

why_the_six_are_not_fixed_yet.next_step: read a second and a third filing the same way - full text, independently located must-include and must-exclude expectations formed before the rule changes - then change the rule.
why_the_six_are_not_fixed_yet.the_available_shortcut_is_wrong: narrowing the scope to Note 16A alone would remove all six in one edit. It would also remove blocks 2302 and 2351 - the contingencies note lead-in and the Seagen legal matters bullet - which this same read confirmed are correctly in scope. A fix that drops confirmed disclosures to reach a count is worse than the defect.
why_the_six_are_not_fixed_yet.what_a_real_fix_needs: a rule for where the audit report ends and the notes begin that holds across filings with different structures. Inventing it from one filing is the mistake this content check exists to catch.
